courses.name: Data Structures and Algorithms
objectives: Explain the fundamental concept of Data Structures and Algorithms.
Emphasize the importance of data structures in designing and implementing efficient algorithms.
prerequisites: Sound knowledge in Python (courses 1008, Introduction to IT systems Lab, and 2131, Programming in Python).
Control structures, modular program design, arrays and functions (courses 2131/2139, Problem Solving and Programming / Lab).

outcomes.title: Illustrate the basic data structure concepts through Python language

modules.title: Describe the concept of algorithm and asymptotic analysis
Demonstrate Recursive Algorithms
Explain Data Structures and its classifications
Illustrate Arrays in Python

outcomes.content: Algorithms: definition, asymptotic analysis, Big-O notation, Big Omega notation and recursion. Data Structures: definition, classification, linear data structures, non-linear data structures and Abstract Data Type (ADT). Arrays: array-based sequences; traverse, insert, delete, search and update; and two-dimensional arrays in Python.

outcomes.title: Use different Searching and Sorting Algorithms

modules.title: Demonstrate Linear search algorithm
Illustrate Binary Search algorithm
Use Bubble Sort algorithm
Apply Selection Sort algorithm
Demonstrate Merge Sort algorithm
Sketch Quick Sort algorithm

outcomes.content: Searching algorithms: Linear Search and Binary Search. Sorting algorithms: Bubble Sort, Selection Sort, Quick Sort and Merge Sort.

outcomes.title: Demonstrate linear data structures Stack, Queue and Linked Lists

modules.title: Demonstrate Array Based Stack ADT operations
Use stack to convert infix expression to postfix expression and evaluate postfix expression
Illustrate Array based Queue ADT
Classify different type of Queues such as circular Queue and Double Ended Queue
Explain Linked list Concept
Demonstrate different types of linked list such as singly linked list, doubly linked list and circular linked list
Implement stack ADT using singly Linked list
Use a Singly Linked List to implement Queue ADT

outcomes.content: Stacks: introduction, ADT, array representation, operations, applications, infix-to-postfix conversion and evaluation of postfix expressions. Queues: introduction, queue ADT, array representation, operations, circular queue and deque types. Linked lists: singly linked lists, memory representation, operations and traversal, circular and doubly linked lists, and linked-list implementations of Stack and Queue.

outcomes.title: Sketch nonlinear Data Structures such as Tree and graph

modules.title: Explain the concepts in Graph data structure and its types
Apply the different representations of a Graph
Demonstrate Graph Traversal algorithms such as BFS and DFS
Describe Tree Data Structure and terminologies related to it
Classify different types of Binary Trees
Use different representations of Binary Tree
Illustrate Different Tree Traversal Algorithms such as Inorder, Preorder and Postorder
Implement Binary Search Tree operations

outcomes.content: Graphs: vertex, edge, adjacent vertices, self-loop, parallel edges, isolated vertex, degree of vertex, pendant vertex, subgraph, paths and cycles; directed, undirected, simple, complete, cyclic, acyclic, bipartite, complete bipartite, connected, disconnected and regular graphs; set, linked and matrix representations; BFS and DFS. Trees: node, parent, child, link, root, leaf, level, height, depth, degree, sibling, ancestor, path and path length; full, complete, strict and perfect binary trees; linked-list representations; inorder, preorder and postorder traversal; and binary-search-tree insertion, traversal, deletion and node counting.

references: Michael T. Goodrich, Roberto Tamassia and Michael H. Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python (An Indian Adaptation), Wiley, 1st edition, July 2021.
Bradley N. Miller, Problem Solving with Algorithms and Data Structures Using Python, Franklin Beedle & Assoc., 2nd edition, January 2013.
